source.title: Studying Small Language Models with Susceptibilities
source.authors: Garrett Baker; George Wang; Jesse Hoogland; Daniel Murfet

record.tranche_reason: The study uses susceptibility-based PCA, rather than a grokking experiment, to check whether a functional circuit is identified across independently trained runs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports susceptibility patterns, functional-head analyses, and training trajectories, but does not measure delayed test generalization or grokking. Those results do not test V1–V5 or V7. The cross-seed induction-circuit result bears on V6.
record.test_reason: This is an interpretability-method paper: it uses SGLD susceptibilities and PCA on a 3M-parameter attention-only language model trained on the Pile. It runs no grokking experiment and does not measure delayed generalization, progress measures, weight-norm effects or optimizer artifacts. The cross-seed result tests whether the authors' own method recovers an induction circuit already identified per seed by Wang et al. (2024). That is the method's performance, not a test of whether networks converge to the same algorithm on a grokking task. Nanda et al. (2023) appears only in a citation list of ablation methods.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that susceptibilities give a principled interpretability tool whose response-matrix PCA separates known functional modules (word segmentation, the induction circuit versus multigram heads, possibly bracket-matching heads) in a 3M-parameter transformer. They note the induction-circuit separation holds across four seeds and is corroborated by trajectory PCA. They draw no conclusion about grokking.
record.recipe_differences: Uses local SGLD susceptibility estimates and PCA to infer model structure; it does not reproduce a grokking training setup or measure delayed generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports variation in susceptibility responses across datasets, heads, contexts, and training checkpoints; it does not report sensitivity of the V6 cross-seed result to architecture or hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Across four seeds of a two-layer attention-only LM, an induction circuit is recovered by susceptibility PCA (positive PC2 loadings). The specific heads filling the previous-token, current-token and induction roles differ between seeds, as identified in the cited Wang et al. (2024).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained small transformers on natural text develop a functionally equivalent induction circuit implemented by different heads across seeds, and susceptibility PCA recovers it.

record.problems: For this claim, the evidence is limited to four seeds of one architecture on one task and does not compare architectures or hyperparameters. The authors also note that SGLD samples are correlated and that the effects of SGLD hyperparameter selection on susceptibility estimates are poorly understood.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly test the listed claim versions. The paper's other susceptibility, ablation-comparison, and trajectory-PCA findings are about interpretability and functional-head structure, not delayed generalization or its proposed mechanisms.

untested.parts: all; no grokking task, and algorithm identity across seeds, architectures or hyperparameters is not measured by the study itself

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' label should be dropped. The study is not about grokking, and its cross-seed result validates the method rather than measuring algorithm convergence. The circuit identities per seed are cited results. No other results bear on V1–V7.

versions.untested_parts: Tests consistency across four random seeds for one architecture and task; does not compare architectures or hyperparameters.

rows.subject: two-layer attention-only transformer (four independently trained seeds; aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: trained on next-token prediction on a subset of the Pile
rows.operation_detail: Per-token susceptibility PCA; checked whether the induction circuit appeared among heads with positive PC2 loadings.
rows.measure: Identification of the induction circuit by positive PC2 head loadings
rows.value: The induction circuit as the heads with positive loadings in PC2 holds across all four independently trained seeds.
rows.note: The paper reports this as an aggregate across four seeds; it does not give a separate numerical score for each seed.
rows.check: The row reports the study's own method recovering a known circuit (positive PC2 loadings) across four seeds, so it is method validation, not a measure of algorithm convergence. Which heads form the induction circuit in each seed comes from the cited Wang et al. (2024), not this study. Those heads differ by seed (e.g. induction head 1:0 in seed 2, 1:6 in seed 3, 1:1 and 1:3 in seed 4). The setting is next-token prediction on natural text, not a grokking task, so it does not bear on V6 as stated for grokking.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Four independently trained seeds of the same two-layer attention-only transformer
reader_labels.reason: Susceptibility PCA identifies the induction circuit in PC2 across all four seeds (r1); architecture and hyperparameters are not varied.
